p: Peter and John went up together: Christ, in healing a man that was born lame and well known to all men, both in a famous place and at a popular time, by the hands of his apostles partly strengthens and encourages those who believed, and partly also calls others to believe.
gave heed unto them: Both with heart and eyes.
held Peter and John: Either because he loved them who had healed him, or because he feared that if he let them go out of his sight that he would become lame again.

And when Peter saw it: Miracles are appointed to convince the unbelievers, and therefore they wickedly abuse the miracles who, standing amazed, either at the miracles themselves or at the instruments and means which is pleases God to use, take an occasion to establish idolatry and superstition by that which God has provided for the knowledge of his true worship, that is, Christianity.
of life: Who has life in himself, and gives life to others.
yea: Because he believed on him who was raised from the dead, whose name he heard about from us.

And now: It is best of all to receive Christ as soon as he is offered to us: but those who have neglected so great a benefit through man's weakness, yet have repentance as a means. As for the shame of the cross, we have to set against that the decree and purpose of God for Christ, foretold by the Prophets, how that first of all he would be crucified here upon the earth, and then he would appear from heaven the judge and restorer of all things, that all believers might be saved, and all unbelievers utterly perish.
by the mouth of all his: Though there were many Prophets, yet he speaks only of one mouth, to show us the consent and agreement of the Prophets.
Whom the heaven must receive until: Or, be taken up into heaven.
A prophet shall the Lord your: This promise referred to an excellent and singular Prophet.
from Samuel and those that follow: At which time the kingdom of Israel was established.
Ye are the: The Jews that believed are the first begotten in the kingdom of God.
children of the prophets: For whom the Prophets were especially appointed.
raised up his Son Jesus: Given to the world, or raised from the dead, and advanced to his kingdom.
